headline: Dry autumn sunshine prevails; Kentucky valleys stay chilly with patchy frost and fog while a cool, breezy Upstate wedge deepens this weekend
disclaimer: Independent amateur analysis. This is not an official forecast or warning. Follow the National Weather Service and local authorities during hazardous weather.

refresh.workflow: Update and commit forecast.json once. GitHub Actions automatically locks the prior issue in forecast-history.json. Then verify the GitHub Pages URL; every Google Sites embed reads the same file and refreshes automatically.

kentucky.name: Central Kentucky
kentucky.subtitle: Danville primary · Lexington comparison
kentucky.summary: Sunny, dry weather continues across Danville and the Bluegrass through Sunday under high pressure. Chilly clear nights favor patchy frost and localized river-valley fog, while daytime temperatures hold near 70. Monday begins in the middle 40s and warms into the lower 60s by the end of this 72-hour forecast.
kentucky.currentConditions: At 1:35 PM EDT, KDVK was clear at 64.4°F with a 41°F dew point and an east wind near 5 kt. At 12:54 PM, KLEX was clear at 68°F with a 45°F dew point and a northeast wind near 8 kt. No precipitation or official NWS alert was present at issuance.

days.label: Friday
days.hazard: No official NWS alert is active for the Danville point. Independent concern is limited to patchy frost and localized valley fog late tonight into early Saturday; a widespread freeze is not expected.
days.forecast: Mostly sunny and dry through the afternoon with a light east breeze. Danville's most likely high is 67°F. Tonight turns clear and chilly; the most likely Danville low is near 40°F, while sheltered rural valleys may briefly reach the middle to upper 30s with patchy frost and localized fog toward daybreak Saturday.

days.label: Saturday
days.hazard: No official NWS alert is active for Saturday at issuance. Patchy valley fog or frost is possible around daybreak Sunday, but no widespread hazardous weather is expected.
days.forecast: Any isolated valley fog or frost dissipates quickly, followed by full sunshine and a very light east wind. Danville's most likely high is 70°F. Saturday night remains clear, with a most likely Danville low near 44°F and a few colder sheltered valleys near 40°F.

days.label: Sunday
days.hazard: No official NWS alert is active for Sunday at issuance, and no significant independent hazard is expected. Localized pre-dawn valley fog remains a low-probability concern.
days.forecast: Sunny and pleasantly mild with a light east wind. Danville's most likely high is 71°F. Sunday night stays clear and cool with a most likely low near 45°F; patchy fog may form in the most sheltered river valleys toward Monday morning. Monday then warms from the middle 40s into roughly 60–64°F by the end of the forecast period.

kentucky.bottomLine: Central Kentucky stays dry and sunny through Sunday. Most likely Danville highs are 67°F, 70°F and 71°F; most likely nighttime lows are 40°F, 44°F and 45°F. Patchy frost or valley fog is possible near daybreak, and Monday warms into the lower 60s by the end of the forecast period. No official alert is active.
kentucky.confidence: High on dry weather and afternoon temperatures; moderate-high on exact valley lows and localized frost or fog placement

upstate.name: Upstate South Carolina
upstate.subtitle: Clemson primary · Central/Pickens County comparison
upstate.summary: Sunny, dry weather continues around Clemson and Central, but a stronger northeast-flow wedge makes Saturday and Sunday cooler and breezier. Afternoon gusts of 18–26 mph are expected both days, remaining below advisory criteria. Monday begins chilly before temperatures rebound toward 70 by the end of this 72-hour forecast.
upstate.currentConditions: At 12:54 PM EDT, KCEU was clear at 66.9°F with a 35°F dew point and an east wind near 7 kt. At 1:35 PM, KLQK was clear at 68.5°F with a 29°F dew point and a southeast wind near 6 kt. The dry air supports a rain-free forecast; Tempest data was not used.

days.label: Friday
days.hazard: No official NWS alert is active for the Clemson point. No significant independent weather hazard is expected today or tonight.
days.forecast: Sunny and dry with a light northeast wind around 3–8 mph. Clemson's most likely high is 70°F. Tonight is mostly clear; the most likely Clemson low is near 48°F, while sheltered Central and Pickens County locations may fall near 40°F.

days.label: Saturday
days.hazard: No official NWS alert is active for Saturday at issuance. The independent concern is a breezy northeast wind with gusts around 18–26 mph; no freeze or widespread frost is expected in the Clemson–Central corridor.
days.forecast: Sunny but cooler as a strong, dry wedge becomes established. Clemson's most likely high is 66°F. Northeast wind runs 8–13 mph with gusts near 18–26 mph. Saturday night stays clear and breezy; Clemson is most likely near 45°F, with sheltered Central and Pickens County locations in the upper 30s.

days.label: Sunday
days.hazard: No official NWS alert is active for Sunday at issuance. Breezy northeast flow remains the independent concern, with gusts around 18–26 mph but below advisory criteria.
days.forecast: Sunny, cool and still breezy beneath the persistent dry wedge. Clemson's most likely high is 65°F. Northeast wind runs 7–12 mph with gusts near 18–26 mph. Sunday night remains clear; Clemson's most likely low is near 45°F while sheltered Central and Pickens County locations fall into the upper 30s. Monday then warms toward 70°F by the end of the forecast period.

upstate.bottomLine: The Clemson–Central corridor remains sunny and dry through Sunday. Most likely Clemson highs are 70°F, 66°F and 65°F; most likely Clemson lows are 48°F, 45°F and 45°F, with sheltered Central and Pickens County locations several degrees colder. Northeast gusts of 18–26 mph are the only notable weekend concern, followed by a Monday rebound toward 70°F.
upstate.confidence: High on dry weather; moderate-high on weekend highs because the current NAM is colder than the GFS and ECMWF guidance

analysisLinks.label: College of DuPage satellite and radar

sourceNotes: No official NWS alert was active for the Danville point at the 17:41Z check or for the Clemson point at the 17:48Z check. Official alerts remain separate from this independent analysis.

The 17:09Z Louisville and 17:31Z Greenville-Spartanburg discussions, official point forecasts, HRRR 12Z, RAP 15Z, NAM and NAM 3-km 12Z, GFS and GEFS 12Z, and ECMWF 06Z agree on a dry 72-hour period. For the Upstate, the current NAM remains colder than the GFS and ECMWF during the weekend; the issued ranges and central values blend that spread without treating any one model as a standalone forecast.

Current KLEX and KGSP BUFKIT profiles were consulted for temperature, inversion and northeast-wind structure. BUFKIT was used as a visualization interface for the underlying HRRR, RAP, NAM and GFS cycles and was not counted as a separate model.

The validated seven-model GRIB package covered 16:15:48Z October 23 through 16:15:48Z October 26. Global and NAM samples extend to 18Z, and the NWS Monday forecast covers the final 1 hour 34 minutes of this later-issued candidate; short-range HRRR, RAP and NAM 3-km guidance is partial at the far end and was not used as full-horizon evidence.
The 17:25Z College of DuPage Ohio River Valley radar showed no coherent precipitation near Central Kentucky, and the 17:26Z infrared frame showed no organized deep cloud shield over the target area.

College of DuPage Southeast radar at 17:45Z showed no coherent precipitation near the Upstate, and the 17:41Z clean-infrared satellite frame showed no organized deep cloud cover over the Clemson–Central corridor.

Chris Bailey's October 23 Kentucky Weather Center post described the dry, pleasant pattern continuing through the weekend and much of next week; its more active Halloween signal lies beyond this 72-hour forecast.

The latest cumulative accuracy summary was consulted: 26 verified forecasts, 70 verified checkpoints and 74.1% all-category accuracy. Station corrections, empirical range widths, regime-specific model weights, fog timing and official-alert handling were applied.

Temperature cards retain calibrated regional coverage ranges, while the prose supplies narrower most-likely Danville and Clemson values. Wider nighttime ranges account for terrain-driven differences between the primary and comparison stations and for colder Kentucky valleys.
Tempest data was not used for Upstate observations, verification, calibration or adjustment.
